implementation_statement: Group POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) applies to the GEPS. GEPS role request and approval procedures are kept by the ERP platform team.

Workforce accounts come from SYS-G1 identity governance driven by HR events; GEPS roles are requested in identity governance and approved by the company-code data owner in each division. Gap: the 6 integration hub service accounts and 14 batch accounts are managed by hand outside identity governance and are not in certification campaigns.
evidence: Identity governance export; GEPS user and service account lists

implementation_statement: Provisioning, disabling, and certification campaigns are automated in SYS-G1 identity governance.

control_name: Automated Temporary and Emergency Account Management
implementation_statement: Temporary and emergency accounts expire automatically (default 30 days).
Accounts inactive for 60 days are disabled automatically; terminated users are disabled within 4 hours of the HR event.
Account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal are logged and sent to the SIEM.
GEPS sessions end after 30 minutes of inactivity; shop-floor GEPS reporting kiosks after 15 minutes.
User behavior analytics in the SIEM flag atypical GEPS use (bulk exports, off-hours mass changes to bills of materials or schedules).
Accounts of individuals HR or security flags as high risk are disabled within 1 hour on request.
GEPS enforces role-based access by company code (Manufacturing, Electric Utility, Grid Engineering, corporate) and by plant. Roles come from the SYS-G1 role catalog.
evidence: GEPS role design; test of 8 roles in P07

implementation_statement: The integration hub is the only approved path between the GEPS and plant MES; flows run through each plant OT DMZ at P1 to P7. Gap: at P8 the hub talks directly to the dual-homed legacy MES server, bypassing any DMZ.
evidence: Integration hub interface list; P8 network diagram

implementation_statement: Segregation-of-duties rules (SOX) block conflicting finance roles. Gap: 11 users hold both storm stock issue (Electric Utility company code) and spare transformer release (Manufacturing company code) roles, so one person can allocate a spare unit and issue it.
Least privilege is applied to workforce roles. Gap: the 6 integration hub service accounts can write work orders to all 8 plant MES instead of one plant each.
Access to security functions (role administration, audit settings) is restricted to named GEPS security administrators through PAM.
Administrators use separate privileged accounts for administrative work.
Privileged GEPS and database access is granted just in time through PAM with approval and session recording.
Privileged and workforce access is certified every quarter (SOX in-scope roles included).
Privileged function use in the GEPS and its database is logged and sent to the SIEM.

control_name: Prohibit Non-privileged Users from Executing Privileged Functions
implementation_statement: Non-privileged users cannot run administrative transactions; the transaction list is enforced by role design.
Sign-in locks after 10 failed attempts; risk-based blocking in SYS-G1.
A system use notice is shown at GEPS sign-in.
Managed workstations lock after 10 minutes idle.
GEPS sessions end after 30 minutes idle and after 10 hours in any case.
Remote workforce access uses SYS-G1 sign-in with MFA over the group zero-trust access service. ERP vendor support connects only through PAM with per-ticket approval and recording.
evidence: Remote access policy; PAM vendor session log

implementation_statement: Remote sessions are logged and monitored in the SIEM.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote access sessions are encrypted (TLS 1.2 or higher).
Use of personal devices and external systems for GEPS data is limited by POL-05; GEPS is reachable only from managed devices.
Sharing of GEPS data with customers and suppliers runs only through EDI and the supplier portal under contract terms.
POL-05 and the group training standard apply.
Annual security awareness training for all workforce users; quarterly phishing exercises.
Insider threat awareness is part of the annual course.
Role-based training for GEPS administrators and key users. Gap: integration hub engineers have no OT-aware training on the plant interfaces.
Training records are kept in the learning system for 6 years.
Group logging standard applies.
The GEPS logs sign-ins, role changes, master data changes (bills of materials, routings, customer and supplier masters), schedule releases, and export screening overrides.
Records include user, time, transaction, object, and before-and-after values for master data.
Log storage in the central archive scales automatically.

control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
implementation_statement: Loss of a log source raises a SIEM alert within 1 hour.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: SOC reviews GEPS security events daily. Gap: APS and integration hub job logs (schedule releases, interface changes) are not sent to the SIEM, so changes to plant work orders are not reviewed.
evidence: SIEM data source list; P07 test

implementation_statement: SIEM correlates and alerts automatically; SOAR opens cases.
Logs from SYS-G1, cloud, EDR, and GEPS are correlated in one SIEM.
All GEPS components use the provider time service.
Logs are written to a separate log archive account with write-once retention.

control_name: Access by Subset of Privileged Users
implementation_statement: Only the SOC log administrators can manage the archive.
1 year searchable and 7 years archived for GEPS audit logs; export screening records kept 7 years in the GEPS (more than the 5 years 15 CFR 762.6 requires).
regulatory_driver: C-CRITICAL-MFG-R03 (15 CFR 762.6(a)) (P03 G-100); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-044)

implementation_statement: Audit generation is on for all GEPS modules and the database.
Group assessment and authorization standard applies.
Group internal audit assesses common controls once a year and samples GEPS controls (P07).
Assessors are independent of the teams that run the controls; OT tests are co-sourced.
Interconnection agreements exist for P1 to P7 MES interfaces and the EDI provider. Gap: no agreement documents the P8 legacy MES connection or 2 direct supplier EDI links.
GEPS weaknesses are tracked in the group POA&M (P07).
Internal authorization decision recorded in section 4.2 of this SSP.
Continuous monitoring of configuration, vulnerabilities, and security events, reported monthly.
The 2026 penetration test covered the GEPS web tier and supplier portal. Gap: the integration hub and its plant interfaces were excluded.
Internal connections between GEPS tiers are documented and limited by network policy.
Group configuration management standard applies.
Baselines for GEPS servers come from group hardened images; GEPS application configuration is version-controlled.
All GEPS changes go through the change advisory board with SOX approvals and testing; emergency changes are reviewed within 2 business days.

control_name: Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes
implementation_statement: Changes are tested in a quality environment before production.
Security impact analysis is part of each change. Gap: interface changes that affect plant MES are not reviewed by plant OT engineers.
Only the release team can move transports to production.
Guardrail policies enforce configuration settings in the GEPS accounts; deviations are reported weekly.
Unneeded services and ports are disabled by image and network policy.
Cloud resources are inventoried automatically. Gap: the interface inventory does not list the P8 legacy MES endpoints or the batch accounts that use them.
The GEPS configuration management plan is part of the platform runbook.
Software license use is tracked centrally.
Users cannot install software on GEPS servers; endpoint controls block unapproved installs.
Group continuity policy (POL-03 and the continuity standard) applies.

The GEPS contingency plan covers database failover and finance recovery. Gap: it does not set the order for restoring APS, the integration hub, and plant interfaces, or how plants re-synchronize their MES after a restore.
The plan is coordinated with the group crisis plan and the P08 runbook.
Plants can work released orders and paper travelers for up to 3 days at P1 to P7. Gap: P8 has no paper procedure.
Recovery staff complete annual contingency training.
Finance modules were restored in provider B in 2026-02. Gap: APS and the integration hub have never been restored in a test, so the 24-hour RTO for scheduling is unproven.
Backups are stored in the immutable vault in provider B, separate from production.
A warm disaster recovery environment in provider B with database replication (RPO about 15 minutes).
Two carriers and cellular backup for plant WAN links.
Daily immutable backups of GEPS databases and application servers to the provider B vault with a separate backup identity.
Backup integrity checks run daily. Gap: restore tests cover finance tables only.
Backups are encrypted with group-managed keys.
Recovery and reconstitution steps exist for the database and finance. Gap: no reconstitution steps for APS schedules and plant interface queues.
Group identity standard applies.
Every GEPS user signs in with a unique SYS-G1 identity.
Phishing-resistant MFA for administrators.
MFA with number matching for all workforce users.
Authentication is replay resistant (modern federation protocols).
Identifiers are unique and never reused.
Workforce authenticators are managed in SYS-G1. Gap: 6 hub service accounts use static keys older than 1 year, stored in the hub configuration.
Password rules follow the group identity standard (length, breached-password screening).
Supplier portal users authenticate with MFA through the group customer identity service.
Re-authentication is required for privileged elevation and every 10 hours.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy applies.
Annual incident response training for responders and liaisons.
Technical playbooks are tested every quarter. Gap: no cross-division exercise that includes plant restart, utility reporting, and the notification matrix has been held.
The group SOC handles GEPS incidents using group playbooks, including the P08 ransomware runbook.
Incidents are tracked in the case system.
Internal reporting within 1 hour is in place. Gap: the multi-regulator notification matrix (P08) has not been exercised.
regulatory_driver: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05; Utility addendum sec. 1 (CIP-013-2 R1.2.1 flow-down) (P03 G-091); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-055)

implementation_statement: Group IR plan v5 covers IT. Gap: it does not yet include the cross-division notification steps or plant restart coordination.
Nonlocal maintenance by the ERP vendor runs through PAM with MFA and recording.
Media sanitization in provider data centers is inherited (provider SOC 2 reports).
Physical access to provider data centers is inherited (provider SOC 2 reports).
Group planning standard applies.
This SSP.
Rules of behavior in POL-05 are acknowledged at hire and every year.
Architecture separates web, application, and database tiers and routes all plant traffic through the hub (except P8, see AC-4).
High baseline selected and tailored (section 6).
Group risk management strategy and acceptance levels (POL-01 4.4).
Background checks for all workforce members before access.
Access disabled within 4 hours of termination.
ERP vendor and integrator personnel requirements are in contracts.
Categorized High (section 6).
Group and division risk assessments (P01) include the GEPS.
Weekly authenticated scans of GEPS hosts; critical findings fixed within 15 days.
Critical components (database, APS, integration hub) identified in the BIA (P05).
ERP and integrator contracts include security requirements and notification terms.
Security engineering principles are applied in design reviews.
Cloud providers and the ERP vendor are assessed yearly (SOC 2 reports reviewed).
All GEPS components run supported versions.
Provider denial-of-service protection on public endpoints.
GEPS sits behind the landing-zone hub and web application firewall; plant flows terminate in OT DMZs. Gap: the P8 path reaches a dual-homed server on the plant network.
External access points are limited to the hub and the supplier portal edge.

control_name: Deny by Default: Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny by default; allow by exception.
All GEPS traffic is encrypted in transit.
TLS 1.2 or higher with approved ciphers.
Customer-managed keys in the provider key service, rotated yearly.
Approved cryptography for data at rest and in transit.
Session tokens are protected and bound to the session.
Databases and storage are encrypted at rest.
Encryption at rest uses group-managed keys.
Security patches for GEPS servers within 15 days for critical; ERP vendor patches each quarter.
EDR on all GEPS servers.
24x7 SOC monitoring with EDR and network detection. Gap: no OT monitoring at P8, and no egress baselines on the integration hub.
Inbound and outbound traffic is inspected at the hub. Gap: hub-to-plant traffic is not baselined.
Security advisories (including CISA ICS advisories for plant interfaces) are reviewed daily.
File integrity monitoring on GEPS application servers; transport packages are signed.
Input validation on interfaces and the supplier portal.
GEPS retention schedule: financial records 7 years, export records 7 years.
regulatory_driver: C-CRITICAL-MFG-R03 (15 CFR 762.6(a)) (P03 G-100); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-022)

implementation_statement: Group supply chain risk management policy (POL-01 4.8).
Group supply chain risk management plan (2025).
Supplier security requirements and covered-equipment checks in purchasing.
Acquisition strategies require supported software and vendor notification terms.
Tier 1 suppliers (ERP vendor, cloud providers, EDI provider) reviewed every year.
ERP vendor and EDI provider contracts require incident notice within 24 hours.
